dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a format object, this projection returns its twelfth field, the real unit roundoff u.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: An m-indexed type of complete computation runs. Its constructor packages a format, two length-m real vectors, scalars bK and c, a summation tree and permutation, a computed numerator and output yHat, and all representability, safe-range, computation, nonzero, and residual-error hypotheses listed in D010.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The universal quantifier ranges only over runs satisfying this extensive packaged specification, rather than over arbitrary numerical data.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: The second field of a run, a vector a : Fin m -> Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its entries occur in the exact products a_i b_i, the sum, the computation assumptions, and the backward-error identity.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: The third field of a run, a vector b : Fin m -> Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its entries occur in the exact products a_i b_i, the sum, the computation assumptions, and the backward-error identity.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: The fourth field of a run, the real scalar bK.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It scales yHat in the general identity, is required to be nonzero by the run specification, and controls the exact bK = 1 special case.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: The fifth field of a run, the real scalar c.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the leading term on the right-hand side of both exact backward-error identities.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: The first field of a run, its abstract floating-point format.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: The seventeenth field of a run, the real computed output yHat.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the output represented by the two perturbed exact identities.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: The abstract format type constructed by D011, containing radix and precision data, representability and safe-range predicates, a rounding map, unit roundoff, and axioms for these objects.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It restricts admissible runs and provides the unit roundoff used in the conclusions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: The run constructor. Given a format F; vectors a and b; reals bK and c; proofs that every a_i and b_i, bK, and c are representable; bK != 0; safeRange(a_i b_i) for every i; a binary tree with m+1 leaves; a permutation of those leaves; validity of the permuted leaf computation; a numerator equal to the rounded tree evaluation; and yHat satisfying yHat = numerator when bK = 1 and yHat = round(numerator/bK), with numerator/bK safe, when bK != 1, it additionally requires the residual bounds |(c - sum_i a_i b_i) - bK*yHat| <= (m+1)u (|bK*yHat| + sum_i |a_i b_i|) and, conditionally on bK = 1, |(c - sum_i a_i b_i) - yHat| <= m u (|yHat| + sum_i |a_i b_i|). It then constructs a run.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: These are all implicit hypotheses carried by run. In particular, the residual inequalities needed for the perturbation conclusions are assumed as fields of every quantified run.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: The format constructor. It takes natural radix beta and precision p, integer exponent bounds emin and emax, with 2 <= beta, 0 < p, and emin < emax; a representability predicate whose represented-real set is finite; a safe-range predicate; a rounding map; and a real u >= 0 satisfying u*(2*(beta as a real)^(p-1)) = 1. It requires 0 and 1 to be representable, safe inputs to round to representable values, round(x) to minimize |x-round(x)| among representable values for every safe x, and every representable x to satisfy round(x) = x.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the admissible abstract arithmetic and constrains u. Radix, precision, exponent bounds, and rounding axioms do not occur directly in the target conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: The eighth format field, the predicate saying that a real number is representable.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It appears only in the packaged format and run admissibility conditions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: The eleventh format field, the rounding function Real -> Real.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014

binders: m is an arbitrary natural number, with m = 0 allowed.
run is an arbitrary admissible computation package of dimension m.
Write F for run's format, a and b for its functions Fin m -> Real, bK and c for its real scalar inputs, N for its numerator, yHat for its computed output, and u for F's unit roundoff.
The run also contains a binary summation tree T with exactly m+1 leaves and a permutation pi of Fin(m+1).
hypotheses: The format has a natural radix beta and precision p and integer exponent bounds emin and emax satisfying 2 <= beta, 0 < p, and emin < emax.
The format supplies predicates representable and safeRange, a rounding map round, and a real u >= 0 satisfying u*(2*beta^(p-1)) = 1, where beta is cast to a real.
The set of representable real numbers is finite; 0 and 1 are representable.
For every safeRange x, round(x) is representable and minimizes |x-round(x)| among all representable real numbers.
Every representable x is fixed exactly by rounding: round(x) = x.
Every a_i and b_i, as well as bK and c, is representable.
For every i in Fin m, the exact product a_i b_i satisfies safeRange.
Define q_i = round(a_i b_i), define x_0 = c and x_(i+1) = -q_i, and feed the permuted vector v_j = x_(pi(j)) to T.
Every leaf value used by T is representable, and recursively at every internal node both child computations are valid and the exact sum of their evaluated values satisfies safeRange.
N equals the evaluation of T on v, where a leaf returns its value and each internal node returns round(leftValue + rightValue).
If bK != 1, then N/bK satisfies safeRange and yHat = round(N/bK).
The packaged general residual bound is |(c - sum_i a_i b_i) - bK*yHat| <= (m+1)u*(|bK*yHat| + sum_i |a_i b_i|).
Conditionally on bK = 1, the package also contains |(c - sum_i a_i b_i) - yHat| <= m*u*(|yHat| + sum_i |a_i b_i|).
conclusions: There exist a real theta0 and a function theta : Fin m -> Real such that |theta0| <= (m+1)u, every |theta_i| <= (m+1)u, and the exact equality (bK*yHat)*(1+theta0) = c - sum_i (a_i*b_i)*(1+theta_i) holds.

Additionally, if bK = 1, then there exist a real theta0 and a function theta : Fin m -> Real such that |theta0| <= m*u, every |theta_i| <= m*u, and the exact equality yHat*(1+theta0) = c - sum_i (a_i*b_i)*(1+theta_i) holds.
mathematical_definitions: Fin m is the index set {0,...,m-1}; every sum in the target is over all of this set.
Absolute-value notation is the ordinary real absolute value. No vector or matrix norm occurs.
The factors m and m+1 in the bounds are cast exactly from natural numbers to real numbers.
The general and bK = 1 conclusions contain separately quantified witnesses; the second pair of witnesses need not equal the first.
The perturbations are multiplicative factors on the exact products a_i b_i and on the output side: each term is multiplied by 1+theta_i, and bK*yHat or yHat is multiplied by 1+theta0.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural dimension m and every packaged admissible rounded computation run described above, two backward-error statements hold simultaneously. In general, the scaled computed output bK*yHat can be multiplied by 1+theta0 and represented exactly as c minus a sum of the exact products a_i b_i, each multiplied by its own factor 1+theta_i, with every perturbation bounded in absolute value by (m+1)u. In the exact special case bK = 1, a potentially different representation exists with the sharper bound m*u and with yHat itself on the left-hand side.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem is universal only over inhabitants of the heavily constrained run type. For any m or data for which no such run package exists, the universal statement has no instance to which it applies.
The residual-error inequalities are assumptions stored in the run, not conclusions derived solely from the tree computation and rounding axioms.
The second backward-error claim is an implication and is vacuous whenever bK != 1. The run separately requires only bK != 0.
When m = 0, Fin m is empty, all indexed conditions are vacuous, and every sum is zero. In the bK = 1 branch the bound m*u is zero, forcing theta0 = 0.
No explicit smallness assumption such as (m+1)u < 1 is encoded.
The proposition does not require 1+theta0 or 1+theta_i to be positive or nonzero.
The general and special existential witnesses need not be unique and need not be related to one another.

The radix and exponent fields are not connected to representable or safeRange beyond the explicitly listed abstract axioms; in particular, no concrete floating-point encoding or overflow/underflow model is specified.
The identity perturbs the exact products a_i b_i, not a_i and b_i separately, and it makes no componentwise claim about perturbations of the original inputs.
There is no forward-error bound for yHat and no assertion that yHat equals the exact unperturbed quotient.
The exact test bK = 1 is real equality; values merely close to 1 receive no special conclusion.
